sentences.text: The genus contains only one species, Scleromochlus taylori, which was named by Arthur Smith Woodward in 1907.
This creature was about 18.1 cm long and possessed long hind legs.
A 2022 interpretation based on a more complete analysis of known remains determined that Scleromochlus was a running animal, either quadrupedal or bipedal.
Fossils of Scleromochlus have been found in the Carnian Lossiemouth Sandstone of Scotland.
Scleromochlus is classified within the unranked order Ornithodira.
It also belongs to the unranked family Pterosauromorpha.
Finally, the animal belongs to the family Scleromochlidae.
Scleromochlus lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, approximately 237 to 205.7 million years ago.
The phylogenetic position of Scleromochlus is debated, with analyses placing it as a basal ornithodiran, a sister-taxon to pterosaurs, or a basal avemetatarsalian outside Ornithodira.
